correctness.rationale: For normalized dx/2 on [-1,1] and integer 0<=ell<h of opposite parity, the L2 orthogonality and vanishing odd fourth mixed terms reduce the normalized fourth moment exactly to Q(s)=A(1-s)^2+B s^2+2Cs(1-s), s the higher monomial L2 energy share. A,B,C are stated rational moment coefficients, with A<B; C-B has numerator -2(2h+1)[2h^2-(10ell+4)h-(2ell+1)], and this polynomial crosses between h=5ell+2 and 5ell+3. Opposite parity excludes 5ell+2. Completing the square when C>B gives exact mixed optimizer s=(C-A)/(2C-A-B) and K=(C^2-AB)/(2C-A-B); when C<B strict endpoint domination forces the pure higher monomial. Same-parity first variation of each pure monomial excludes pure maxima; the ell=0 constant case is handled by B>1. Dividing moments by ell yields the stated asymptotic h/ell=5 switch. Independent exact rational moment calculations checked 694 opposite-parity exponent pairs; finite tests are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: Two highly relevant primary full texts were inspected. Borwein-Erdelyi-Zhang (1994) studies Müntz-Legendre orthogonalization, derivative bounds, Markov and bounded Nikolskii-type inequalities, but not the exact real L2-to-L4 norm for an opposite-parity two-monomial subspace. Borwein-Erdelyi (1995) treats density/Remez inequalities, not this optimization. Indexed Resultary sharp fourth-moment statements concern Fourier characters and other structures, not two real monomials. The elementary moment quadratic is acknowledged as standard; the exact integer threshold and complete equality classification were not found in these sources.
residual_risks: The quadratic moment maximization is accessible to direct calculation, so an older unindexed sharp two-term Nikolskii exercise could contain the same fivefold threshold.
Same-parity sharp constants remain unsolved here; only the non-pure optimizer necessity is established.

evidence: Theorem 3.4 is an L2 Markov bound; Corollary 3.3 concerns pointwise/L2 bounds, not the best L4 norm of two monomials on a symmetric interval.

value.rationale: Sharp finite-dimensional L2-to-L4 embedding constants are natural approximation/functional-analysis invariants. The integer gap threshold h near 5ell and its distinct mixed/pure extremizer types provide a non-obvious complete parameter classification for two-dimensional Müntz subspaces, including an asymptotic phase boundary. This is mathematically useful despite the elementary exact-moment method and despite not solving the same-parity constant.

limitations: No closed same-parity norm is asserted.
The result does not include complex coefficients, arbitrary measures or higher-dimensional Müntz spaces.
